stories.title: Tag suggestions from page content in the save step
stories.userStory: As a bookmark owner, I want tag suggestions based on what the saved page actually says, so that my bookmarks get useful tags without me typing them by hand.
acceptanceCriteria: When the feature is enabled, saving a link reads the fetched page text with a local model and returns suggested tags alongside the existing auto tags
Suggested tags are never applied automatically; they wait for the user to accept them, and they never replace or change tags the user has typed
The model runs locally on the server; no page content or notes leave the server
A small local model with a timeout computes the suggestions, so a slow or failing model never stalls or breaks the save step
The feature is off by default from its first release, on a fresh install and after an upgrade, and with it disabled saving a link behaves exactly as it does today, including the existing auto tags

demoPoint.description: The Judge watches the automated check run: a saved link comes back with suggested tags next to the existing auto tags, any tag the user typed stays exactly as typed, and a slow or unavailable model only delays suggestions, never the save itself.

featureContract.feature: Tag suggestions from page content in the save step
shouldDo: Suggest tags for a link being saved by reading the fetched page text, not just the URL
Compute the suggestions in the same place auto tags come from, with a small local model behind a timeout so a slow model cannot stall the save step
Return the suggestions alongside the existing automatic tags
Keep every suggestion optional until the user accepts it
Run the model locally on the server
Land off by default behind a minimal instance setting from the first release, before the full switch UI exists
shouldNotDo: Never apply a suggested tag without a user action
Never change or replace a tag the user typed
Never send page content or notes to an outside service
Never change existing auto-tagging rules or the search syntax
Never let the model block or fail the save step

stories.title: The AI switch and editable suggestions on the save page
stories.userStory: As a self-hosting bookmark owner, I want AI tag suggestions to stay off until I turn them on and to edit them on the save page, so that I stay in control of my tags and my server.
acceptanceCriteria: The feature is off by default on a fresh install and after an upgrade
An instance owner can switch it off for everyone, and a user can switch it off for themselves; when the instance is off, no user sees suggestions
Both switches are respected everywhere suggestions appear: the web save page and the check endpoint used by the browser extension and API clients
The save page shows suggested tags that the user can accept, edit or drop one by one before saving
Turning the feature on or off leaves existing auto-tagging rules and search behaviour unchanged

demoPoint.description: The Judge sees the save page twice: with the feature off it looks exactly as today with no suggestions, and with it switched on a short list of suggested tags appears, each one editable or removable before saving.

featureContract.feature: Off-by-default switch and editable suggestions on the save page
shouldDo: Keep AI tag suggestions off until they are switched on, with one clear instance-level switch plus a per-user switch
Respect both switches everywhere suggestions surface: the web save page and the check endpoint used by the browser extension and API clients
Show suggested tags on the save page so the user can accept, edit or drop each one before saving
shouldNotDo: Never turn the feature on by default on a fresh install or upgrade
Never apply a suggestion without a user action
Never hide or alter the existing tag input and the existing auto tags
Never overwrite or auto-edit tags the user typed

sprintPlan.goal: Saving a link with AI suggestions switched on shows editable tag suggestions drawn from the page's own content, while everything stays off by default until the instance or the user turns it on.

checklist: The save-time-tags acceptance check passes in the Verifier
With the feature off, saving a link behaves exactly as today and existing auto tags are unchanged
No suggested tag is ever applied, and none ever replaces a user-entered tag, without an explicit user action
A slow or unavailable model never blocks saving: the suggestion step times out and saving proceeds as today
All suggestions come from a local model on the server; no page content or notes leave the instance
Existing auto-tagging rules and the search syntax are unchanged
The feature is off by default on a fresh install and after an upgrade, from the first release onward

feasibility.concerns: Local model inference on the web request path may slow every save; better to compute suggestions in the same place auto tags come from and keep the model small, with a timeout.
feasibility.conditions: Never auto-apply or override user-entered tags; feature off by default.

feasibility.concerns: Needs changes across settings storage, API check endpoint and the save page UI; medium because both instance-level and per-user switches must be respected everywhere suggestions surface (web and API clients).
feasibility.conditions: Instance owner kill-switch overrides user opt-in.

risk.concerns: Local model adds latency and memory load on small self-hosted instances.
risk.risk: A local model reading full page text on every save slows the save step and touches private bookmark content.
risk.conditions: Model runs locally, feature off by default, suggestions never auto-applied and never replace user-entered tags.

risk.concerns: Two switches (owner and user) must interact safely; editing flow must not silently apply suggestions on save.
risk.risk: Confusing toggles could leave the feature on without users realizing it, and noisy suggestions could override entered tags in the UI.
risk.conditions: One clear switch, off by default; entered tags are never overwritten or auto-edited by suggestions.

facilitatorNote: Kept S1 and S2 with their order and ids. Added to S1: a small model behind a timeout so a slow model cannot stall the save step, and landing off by default behind a minimal instance setting from day one. Extended S2: the instance switch and per-user switch are respected on the save page and on the check endpoint used by the browser extension and API clients. No merges or drops.
